So does this supersede #72475?

Edit: Also, what's the advantage of having ANGLE on Windows?

> So does this supersede #72475?
> 
> Edit: Also, what's the advantage of having ANGLE on Windows?

OpenGL drivers on Windows are all over the place. On many Windows devices OpenGL drivers are so bad that the driver itself produces regular stutters during gameplay.

> So does this supersede https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72475?

Yes, when it's finished.

> Edit: Also, what's the advantage of having ANGLE on Windows?

Some Intel GPUs have much better DX support than OpenGL.

> please note that, mostly due to rebasing, I've had to fix some things. You can see the latest changes here: 

I have synced it a few times, version it this PR seems to be up-to-date, but have a few changes to support ANGLE (includes, moving some attributes for hard-coded to overloaded functions, EGL_ANDROID_blob_cache handling).

> Also note that I've never got to try the DRI_PRIME detection code, so I have no idea if it works (I've just adapted it from the original GL manager one). It might be a good idea to try it out before merging.

Since this PR is only for macOS and Windows, and X11 code use GLX not EGL it's not used at all.

> Reduz has suggested in the chat that he thinks that we should have a fallback on Windows so when OpenGL 3.3 is not supported, we automatically fallback to ANGLE over DX. Do you think doing so will be possible?

Added fallback code for Windows.

> As I think it would be very complex to ship separate versions of the editor and templates with a DLL

What's complex about adding DLLs? There's no need for separate editor or template versions, just adding a DLLs to existing. And the editor is already shipped as ZIP with multiple files, so pretty much nothing changes. Exports targeting Vulcan won't have DLL included.

> How difficult would this be?

Probably will require a modified ANGLE build with mangled function names, or/and custom loader instead of GLAD.

> >  How difficult would this be?
>
> Probably will require a modified ANGLE build with mangled function names, or/and custom loader instead of GLAD.

Actually, only a custom loader should be fine.

Like changing definition of every GL/GLES function in the GLAD headers from:
```c++
GLAD_API_CALL PFNGLDEPTHFUNCPROC glad_glDepthFunc;
#define glDepthFunc glad_glDepthFunc
```
to:
```c++
GLAD_API_CALL PFNGLDEPTHFUNCPROC glad_glDepthFunc;
PFNGLDEPTHFUNCPROC static_glDepthFunc = glDepthFunc;
#undef glDepthFunc;
#define glDepthFunc glad_glDepthFunc
```

And adding a load function to restore functions from the static lib:
```c++
GLAD_API_CALL int gladLoadGLES2Static() {
	...
	glad_glDepthFunc = static_glDepthFunc;
	...
}
```

I'll check if it works.

@bruvzg

> I have synced it a few times, version it this PR seems to be up-to-date, but have a few changes to support ANGLE (includes, moving some attributes for hard-coded to overloaded functions, EGL_ANDROID_blob_cache handling).

It doesn't look like it. This might be because the changes I made were made in the Wayland branch, sorry, I never got to update the main EGL PR.

> Since this PR is only for macOS and Windows, and X11 code use GLX not EGL it's not used at all.

Oh. Are you saying that this is exclusive to Linux or GLX itself?

> What's complex about adding DLLs? There's no need for separate editor or template versions, just adding a DLLs to existing. And the editor is already shipped as ZIP with multiple files, so pretty much nothing changes. Exports targeting Vulcan won't have DLL included.

The main downside about the DLL is that if you double-click the executable while it's in the ZIP archive, then the DLL won't be found. This also applies to any file the executable depends on within the ZIP archive.

Recent Windows 10/11 versions warn you when trying to run an executable from a ZIP file for this reason, but some people may ignore that warning.

> Actually, only a custom loader should be fine.

Tried to do it, I pretty sure it would work, but I do not think it's possible to build ANGLE as static library in a first place.

> Tried to do it, I pretty sure it would work, but I do not think it's possible to build ANGLE as static library in a first place.

OK, seems like `vcpkg` packages include some patches to enable static build for ANGLE, and I got it working with libs from it. Will clean it up and update PR a bit later.

> It doesn't look like it. This might be because the changes I made were made in the Wayland branch, sorry, I never got to update the main EGL PR.

I do not see any relevant changes in the Wayland branch either, please be more specific.

> Oh. Are you saying that this is exclusive to Linux or GLX itself?

I'm saying this PR is not changing Linux code, so `EGLManager` and `detect_prime_egl` are not used on Linux at all, it's using old GLX code in the `platform\linuxbsd`.

> I do not see any relevant changes in the Wayland branch either, please be more specific.

Sorry. I did three other commits after merging, which can be seen here: https://github.com/Riteo/godot/commits/wayland/drivers/egl

Although those are for PRIME detection. That might be why you couldn't find them.

> I'm saying this PR is not changing Linux code, so EGLManager and detect_prime_egl are not used on Linux at all, it's using old GLX code in the platform\linuxbsd.

Yeah that makes sense. I'm a bit worried by the fact that it's unused (for now) and untested code though. Perhaps we should remove it? I can always make a PR for when it's actually tested and used.

Thinking about it it's also probably linuxbsd specific so perhaps it shouldn't be there in the first place.

> Perhaps we should remove it?

Indeed, it probably should not be here, I have removed it.

Now ANGLE is included in `thridparty` folder and statically linked by default on both macOS and Windows (can be overridden by `angle_static=no` flag to revert to dynamic loading). No external dependencies are required to build.

---

Stripped editor binary size increased by about 8 MB (to 128 MB).

Had to change target Windows version from 7 to 8.1 since ANGLE require DirectX 11 support in the SDK. And add a few small patches to fix build with MinGW.

Note: also I had to disable debug symbols for the ANGLE part (is not using `separate_debug_symbols` or MSVC) since Windows have executable size limit of 2 GB and editor build with ANGLE and full debug info it's over that limit (it's still 1.91 GB even in this config).

@bruvzg I think the production team may need to give feedback on this one, but I think it may be better to just have our fork of Angle with the required changes and the ability to generate a `.lib` that can be linked statically, given we don't need to build it for all platforms and its easier to keep up to date.

> I think the production team may need to give feedback on this one, but I think it may be better to just have our fork of Angle with the required changes and the ability to generate a .lib that can be linked statically

CI seems to consistently run out of space, it this like will be necessary in any case.

*Edit:* https://github.com/bruvzg/godot-angle-static, I'll add README for the custom build script (scons with nostly the same args as the engine) and update this PR tomorrow.

Moved ANGLE fork to the https://github.com/bruvzg/godot-angle-static (use Scons with the same args as Godot to build libs, [pre-built libs](https://github.com/bruvzg/godot-angle-static/releases/tag/chromium%2F5908)).

Path to the static libs can be set via `angle_libs=PATH` build flag, if not set dynamic loading is used.
@bruvzg Wow you are awesome!
Tested on Windows. It works great! I downloaded the pre built libs and they worked great.

> Had to change target Windows version from 7 to 8.1 since ANGLE require DirectX 11 support in the SDK. And add a few small patches to fix build with MinGW.

Changed back to Windows 7 for engine build, Windows 8.1 SDK is only necessary to build ANGLE static libs.

Tested successfully on Windows 10 with https://github.com/team-godog/NGJ2023_Godog (after converting the game to GL Compat backend), compiling with VS 2022.

It seems to work well, both out of the box, and with the `angle_libs` path at compile time.

Out of the box, it uses ANGLE provided by Windows:
```
OpenGL API OpenGL ES 3.0.0 (ANGLE 2.1.18912 git hash: 872d7947bb76) - Compatibil
ity - Using Device: Google Inc. (AMD) - ANGLE (AMD, Radeon RX Vega Direct3D11 vs
_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11-31.0.21029.1006)
```

With the static libs, it uses our own version:
```
OpenGL API OpenGL ES 3.0.0 (ANGLE 2.1.21553 git hash: 430a4f559cbc) - Compatibil
ity - Using Device: Google Inc. (AMD) - ANGLE (AMD, Radeon RX Vega Direct3D11 vs
_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11-31.0.21029.1006)
```

Could be worse adding something to disambiguate so we can know easily in logs if we're using the system or bundled ANGLE, the only difference here seems to be the version / git hash.

Did some light testing on Linux, didn't spot regressions in the GL renderer.

> With the static libs, it uses our own version:

> OpenGL API OpenGL ES 3.0.0 (ANGLE 2.1.21553 git hash: 430a4f559cbc) - Compatibil
> ity - Using Device: Google Inc. (AMD) - ANGLE (AMD, Radeon RX Vega Direct3D11 vs
> _5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11-31.0.21029.1006)

So actually, with our static libs I get much worse performance on this demo compared to the system ANGLE.

With the Windows 10 builtin ANGLE, I get 140-160 FPS (vsync disabled), and with our static libs I get 75 FPS.

With native OpenGL, I get 400-430 FPS.
Thanks! Amazing work :tada:

for posteriority: a quick test can be done by placing e.g.
```
[rendering]
renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"
gl_compatibility/driver.windows="opengl3_angle"
```
in the `project.godot`; regardless of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/65541 I couldn't find driver selection settings in the editor's UI menus.

Also, FWIW, this (i.e. switching to ANGLE-based OpenGL renderer) actually fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/60967 for me :)
